public_rationale: Sutton's September 2025 interview was framed around his view that LLMs are a dead end. In November 2025, Sutskever said current models 'generalize dramatically worse than people' and called this 'a very fundamental thing.' A 2025 AAAI survey of 475 participants, mostly academics, found that 76% thought scaling current AI approaches was unlikely to produce AGI. That is roughly 360 people, which fits 'hundreds of researchers.' Each part of the claim is backed by public evidence from the year before the post.
limitations: Sutskever doubts that scaling current models is enough, but he does not reject LLMs outright. 'Huge doubts' is a fair summary but not his own wording.
The survey measured doubts about reaching AGI by scaling, not about LLMs in every respect.
The Sutton evidence is the interviewer's summary of his position.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus and hundreds of other AI researchers, including Sutskever and Sutton, have serious doubts about LLMs.

statement.excerpt: And it goes without saying that I too have huge doubts about LLMs. At this point so do literally hundreds of other researchers, even prominent machine learning insiders like Sutskever and Sutton.

from_speaker: I too have huge doubts about LLMs

our_interpretation: Plain reading: by early January 2026, Sutskever and Sutton had each publicly voiced serious doubts about LLMs, or about scaling the current LLM approach, and at least a few hundred other AI researchers had done the same.
Marcus's own doubts are taken as given. His own writing is not used as evidence.
A survey in which hundreds of researchers say scaling current approaches is unlikely to reach AGI counts as 'hundreds of researchers' with serious doubts about LLMs.
criteria.support_condition: Public statements from Sutskever and Sutton that voice basic limits of LLMs, plus evidence that hundreds of researchers share such doubts, all made in roughly the year before the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Sutskever or Sutton publicly holding that current LLMs face no basic limits, or no evidence that more than a handful of researchers share such doubts.
